question: Which structures of our problem does {3,6}_{(2,0)} represent faithfully, which require choices, and which are lost?
current_assessment: An exact A4-equivariant representation of the declared twelve-channel field and its comparisons, with B recovered from realized left-face sectors. This does not identify torus topology, native histories, or dual endpoint incidence with the original structures.

semantics.supported: The stated scoped claim has the linked checked construction; not a probability of a stronger claim.
semantics.rejected: The stated candidate class has a recorded obstruction; not a rejection of every toroidal realization.
semantics.open: A proposition with an explicit discriminator; neither anticipated success nor anticipated failure.
semantics.requires: Readiness dependencies with required verdicts, not logical implication or automatic promotion.
semantics.priority: Qualitative expected information gain relative to effort; not a physical energy or numerical success probability.
semantics.spatial_quotient: Only lattice addresses are reduced modulo two. Absolute realization origin and full coefficient history are retained.
semantics.basis_changes: Coordinate identifications, admitted native automorphisms and geometric collapses are distinct. H has determinant -1 and is not a new native mirror law.

Chamon-foliation-paper.role: Existing tetrahedral-octahedral gauge model, explicit polynomial Clifford map and entanglement renormalization; Section III.D, IV and Appendices B-C inspected.

Chamon-TDN-paper.role: Existing Chamon topological defect network on tetrahedral-octahedral strata; Section VI.C inspected for cell and interface rules.

Chamon-decoder-source.role: Publisher-linked implementation. README, binary stabilizer builder and coordinate conversion code inspected; Pinned functions executed through the minimal local adapter; 236 support rows agree. Source identifiers and execution scope are recorded in the benchmark note.

Chamon-paper.role: Fontana and Pereira, Boundary Modes in the Chamon Model, v2. Equations 1-6 supply the lattice benchmark; 37-43 and 64-67 supply the boundary-field targets. Source for proposed tests, not a local verification receipt.

paper.role: Monson and Ivic Weiss, 1999: classification and the tetrahedral/cube dual alternatives. Numerical checks below are local reconstructions, not verification of the whole paper.

conjectures.statement: The oriented four-class triangular torus supplies the same twelve endpoint channels and proper A4 action.
conjectures.scope: Directions e1, e2-e1, -e2; selected A4 subgroup, not the full map group.
conjectures.reopen: Change the arrow orientation, endpoint binding, or selected symmetry group.

conjectures.statement: The toroidal channel encoding preserves the supplied field metric and L, G, C.
conjectures.scope: Complex three-component fibers; not the flat positional metric or an identification of the two C3 operations.
conjectures.reopen: Change the field metric, fiber action or named operator conventions.

conjectures.statement: The explicit tetrahedral realization and left-face centroid sectors recover B and B*B.
conjectures.scope: Fixed vertex naming and declared orthogonal map H with determinant -1; cyclic-mode and orientation choices remain explicit.
conjectures.reopen: Change the realization, normalization, left-face convention or meaning of admitted coordinate changes.

conjectures.statement: The original ordered-parent comparison encoding is equivariant for all twelve references and twelve A4 actions.
conjectures.scope: The existing 137-slot protocol is retained; torus faces are not substituted for comparison slots.
conjectures.reopen: Change the reference policy, ordered-parent rules or state/source grouping.

conjectures.statement: The torus realization is a cell-complex isomorphism onto the tetrahedral boundary.
conjectures.scope: The four-vertex, twelve-edge, eight-face torus versus the ordinary tetrahedral boundary.
conjectures.reopen: Only by changing the proposed equivalence or its objects; changing a drawing is insufficient.

conjectures.statement: Reverse-labelled channels can close on the torus with nonzero lifted displacement, so endpoint correspondence alone does not preserve path homotopy.
conjectures.scope: Twelve two-channel return examples; no native transfer is identified with these loops by this statement.
conjectures.reopen: Supply a path-lift convention or change which path information the task retains.

conjectures.statement: The collapsed dual tetrahedron reproduces -B in the common coordinate frame and has a two-to-one dual vertex map.
conjectures.scope: A geometric collapse, not an embedding of all eight dual vertices.
conjectures.reopen: Require injective dual vertices, or change the realization or field-frame recipe.

conjectures.statement: The alternative cube/Petrie realization retains the eight dual vertices and the full group of order 48.
conjectures.scope: Four skew hexagonal faces, not the six ordinary square faces of a cube or a smooth embedded torus.
conjectures.reopen: Change the dual face incidence or vertex map.

conjectures.statement: The faithful cube dual reproduces invertible B using the same face-centroid/edge-endpoint recipe.
conjectures.scope: All twelve frames have rank two because their Petrie hexagon centroid is zero.
conjectures.reopen: Declare a different frame recipe; that is a different candidate, not a reversal of this result.

conjectures.statement: Primal-dual channel permutation preserves the field metric, L, G, C and A4 equivariance.
conjectures.scope: The broader category allowing arbitrary channel permutations.
conjectures.reopen: Change the dual channel orientation or operator data.

conjectures.statement: That channel duality is induced by a permutation of the four primal endpoints and preserves their source fibers.
conjectures.scope: The original typed endpoint category, not decode/re-encode transport into a differently typed presentation.
conjectures.reopen: Change the category to admit a specified reorganization of source/state fibers.

conjectures.statement: A fixed injective complex-linear five-coefficient binding intertwines the declared N permutation with identity transport in the ordered corner frame.
conjectures.scope: Imported existing obstruction: maximum rank three; phase-dependent bindings are a separate class and are nonunique.
conjectures.reopen: Change the fixed-binding requirement, operation or coefficient category.

conjectures.statement: A metric-unitary role-exchanging PN map intertwines the supplied geometric C3 actions.
conjectures.scope: Imported restricted-character obstruction for that named geometric action; an internal target action is a different proposal.
conjectures.reopen: Explicitly change the role-exchange requirement or target action, not merely its name.

conjectures.statement: The FCC quotient by 2 Z3 gives four classes and the required affine A4 channel action, preserving the unrefined honeycomb geometry.
conjectures.scope: The finite affine torus action differs from the proper root-tetrahedron rotation action; cover translations retain deck displacement.
conjectures.reopen: Change the quotient lattice, cell templates or action.

conjectures.statement: The existing fixed octahedral subdivision retains the full tested A4 action.
conjectures.scope: Four of twelve elements preserve it; the remaining eight move its chosen diagonal.
conjectures.reopen: Declare a different subdivision or retain a refinement-choice index.

conjectures.statement: The three diagonal subdivisions form an equivariant geometric family.
conjectures.scope: Alternative subdivisions, not simultaneous occupancy or admitted native moves between them.
conjectures.reopen: Change the primitive family or prescribe a native refinement transport.

conjectures.statement: One unchanged global B realizes all affine FCC torus actions as actual Euclidean vector motions.
conjectures.scope: The nine nonzero translation-class elements fail that square; a translation is not the root rotation with the same endpoint permutation.
conjectures.reopen: Retain pose-dependent frames or change the meaning of the spatial action.

conjectures.statement: Frames independently rebuilt from transformed cells and centers preserve the metric and all twelve field-action squares.
conjectures.scope: Explicit factor-two field-unit normalization, proper coordinate identification and transported named operators; not a five-coefficient native transfer proof.
conjectures.reopen: Change the field units, anchoring, frame recipe or named operator transport.

conjectures.statement: The invariant center-star octahedral subdivision is already a primitive subdivision of the current native grammar.
conjectures.scope: It introduces a non-FCC center and eight tetrahedra instead of the four source components. Geometric validity is not native admission.
conjectures.reopen: An explicit primitive-grammar revision is authorized and separately evaluated.

conjectures.statement: An eight-sector indexed comparison interface preserves the supplied neutron coefficients, field norm and original reader records across the refinement family.
conjectures.scope: Read-only sum/difference charts: four actual available N reader contexts, both explicit phase-aware binding seeds, independent records and a coherent NN-chain fixture. Sector-index A4 and affine pose covariance are tested separately from uniform N field operators; no new native target readers or refinement-changing constructor are admitted.
conjectures.reopen: The retained task, binding family, allowed sidecar, field action or primitive grammar changes.

conjectures.statement: The four coarse averages alone suffice for reversible comparison across all three native-diagonal refinement charts.
conjectures.scope: The declared independent coefficient-record task; the coherent NN-chain fixture is a special subspace with vanishing differences.
conjectures.reopen: Retain differences or restrict the input task to a specified subspace.

conjectures.statement: Every native NN channel map remains supported on at most two target coarse pairs after the declared refinement-chart changes.
conjectures.scope: Three actual NN steps, their co-moving phase-aware field bindings and the explicitly constructed complete charts. Some transported maps touch all four target pairs; the whole operation still stays within the octahedral comparison workspace.
conjectures.reopen: Change the locality unit, channel representation or retained operation.

conjectures.statement: The actual FCC vertex and octahedron incidence supports the Chamon stabilizer Hamiltonian with the expected periodic ground space.
conjectures.scope: External spin-1/2 layer on actual unsplit octahedra; tested physical covers 2x2x2, 4x4x4, 6x6x6 and 4x6x8. Four parity classes label sites on the cover. Native grammar and coefficient meanings are unchanged.

references.location: create_chamon_stabs(2,2,2) and coordinate conversion functions; independent support-matrix reference

conjectures.completed_test: Adapt the inspected existing stabilizer and coordinate routines as an independent reference. Generate a period-four cube from the actual FCC geometry; encode each six-site XXYYZZ stabilizer as a signed binary symplectic Pauli word. Check commutation, squares, four class-product identities, stabilizer rank and absence of minus identity. Run the period-two collapse as a control.
conjectures.acceptance: Period four has 32 spins, 32 commuting stabilizers, binary rank 24, no minus identity and ground-space dimension 256. Period two identifies opposite vertices and makes each stabilizer identity. Odd center classes match the even vertex classes under the declared shift 111.
conjectures.falsifier: The actual incidence produces a wrong support, noncommuting pair, inconsistent stabilizer phase, wrong rank or failure of the class dictionary.
conjectures.reopen: Change the lattice units, periodic cover, stabilizer assignment or boundary conditions.

conjectures.statement: The published Chamon Laurent stabilizer column matches the signed native FCC operators through an explicit primitive-coordinate, anchor and Pauli-frame dictionary.
conjectures.scope: Shirley-Liu-Dua Eq. C1, 240 octahedra on four covers, and the formal Laurent commutation identity. Physical metric and primitive period generators are retained. This is the one-generator column, not the full Appendix B gauge-to-Chamon circuit.

references.location: Appendix C, Eq. C1; explicit native-to-paper dictionary in the local benchmark receipt

conjectures.reopen: Change the primitive coordinates, check anchor, Pauli frame, polynomial convention or periodic quotient.

conjectures.statement: The Chamon operator algebra on our FCC support admits the paired spatial and Pauli-frame actions corresponding to the selected tetrahedral symmetry.
conjectures.scope: Proper root rotations are checked separately from affine translations on the periodic cover. Cover translations retain their deck information; scalar phases of Hilbert-space implementers are recorded separately from conjugation on Pauli operators.

references.location: Section 2, equation 1; spatial/internal symmetry test constructed locally
Section II tetrahedral point symmetry and lattice-coordinate convention; Appendix B operator algebra

conjectures.next_test: Construct the spatial generator actions and internal Clifford conjugations, including rho paired with X to Y to Z to X. Verify every stabilizer image and generator relation. For affine representatives, compare composition with the retained deck translation instead of forcing an order-two cover translation.
conjectures.acceptance: The signed Pauli algebra and Hamiltonian are preserved; all group or lifted-composition relations hold with explicit frame and phase conventions.
conjectures.falsifier: A transformed stabilizer has an unmatched Pauli label or sign, or a composition relation fails after its declared deck and phase factors are included.
conjectures.reopen: Change the selected symmetry, cover, internal action or equivalence of implementer phases.

conjectures.statement: Our FCC incidence reproduces the Chamon four-class defect parities, face-diagonal dipole transport and boundary conversion rules.
conjectures.scope: Binary stabilizer syndromes in the bulk and the z<=0 half-space with five-site boundary stabilizers. Boundary class labels remain those of the paper's odd-center coset.
conjectures.next_test: Enumerate single-spin syndromes, build explicit ribbon and tetrahedral-cage Pauli words, and truncate to the z=0 boundary by the prescribed frozen-spin projection. Check the AB/CD parity distinction, dipole-to-boundary-fracton endpoints and reflection processes; compare the boundary shifted to z=-1.
conjectures.acceptance: Bulk words obey all four class parities; boundary words exhibit the specified surviving and broken parities and the listed endpoint fusion rules, without residual bulk defects in the half-cage tests.
conjectures.falsifier: A purported motion or fusion word leaves additional defects, violates a surviving parity, or fails after shifting the boundary with its class labels retained.
conjectures.reopen: Change the boundary orientation, termination, spin projection or excitation dictionary.

conjectures.statement: A complete indexed refinement presentation preserves the Chamon Pauli algebra, stabilizers and syndromes while using the same physical vertex spins.
conjectures.scope: Exact Appendix B Laurent map and declared signed notebook lift, with six gauge-edge qubits and two explicit ancillas per enlarged cell. All four existing charts preserve operator records on physical covers 4^3, 4x4x8 and 8^3. Shared vertices remain single qubits; no center spin is added. This does not identify qubits with geometric sectors, derive a neutron-field coupling, or claim a fixed-wire finite-depth circuit after discarding the retained translation.

references.location: Exact matrix import, signed finite-cover lift, honeycomb incidence and operator-valued chart multiplication
Section III.D, Appendix B: explicit Pauli algebra map; Section IV and Appendix C: retained toric-code layers
Section VI.C: tetrahedral-octahedral strata, interface conditions and four-charge edge condensates

conjectures.completed_test: Extract the existing polynomial Clifford map and honeycomb gluing dictionary, recording their ancillas and unit-cell change. Specify the sector records and their shared-vertex identifications. Transport observables through all three diagonal charts with sums and differences retained. Test Pauli multiplication, phases, commutators, the six-site stabilizer and its syndrome map; separately test the average-only reduction.
conjectures.acceptance: Complete chart round trips preserve the operator algebra and ground-space constraints with unchanged qubit count; cross-sector products required by a stabilizer remain recoverable.
conjectures.falsifier: A product or stabilizer phase is lost, a shared vertex is duplicated into independent spins, or a chart change preserves vector coefficients but fails the declared operator multiplication.
conjectures.reopen: Change the retained operator algebra, sector encoding, multiplication law or admissible auxiliary data.

conjectures.statement: Retained sector mean/difference data support a discrete boundary-field construction reproducing the Chamon normal-derivative coupling and dipole endpoint charges.
conjectures.scope: Declare a two-component compact boundary field and its symplectic data. The comparison metric is not substituted for the paper's antisymmetric K matrix. Any embedding into existing field components must be named explicitly.
conjectures.next_test: Use the exact sector centroids and spacing to normalize the difference as a discrete normal derivative. Specify the two boundary fields, compactification and antisymmetric bracket; construct the discrete Dxy operator and boundary condition relating the normal derivative to the fields. Match line-operator endpoint charges against the checked lattice fusion words.
conjectures.acceptance: The discrete action and brackets have the stated Chamon boundary form in the continuum limit, and the same retained difference data reproduce the lattice endpoint charges with explicit normalization and boundary choice.
conjectures.falsifier: The boundary bracket is degenerate or wrongly normalized, the difference data cannot encode the required independent modes, or an endpoint charge disagrees with the lattice syndrome.
conjectures.reopen: Change the boundary-field embedding, compactification, symplectic form, derivative stencil or boundary condition.

conjectures.statement: The native P reader task admits a coefficient-compatible toroidal lift retaining deck displacement and absolute origin.
conjectures.scope: Start with the source P advance four-vertex permutation (2,3,0,1), represented on the four classes by translation e2. Do not assert uniqueness of its planar lift.
conjectures.next_test: Use the existing five-to-36 coefficient interface and actual P reader witness. Check one and two advances, all coefficient coordinates, field realization squares, deck displacement and origin separately. Compare quotient-only and retained-lift presentations on the same history.
conjectures.acceptance: An explicit task/operation diagram commutes and recovers coefficients and retained history; two advances retain origin +2 and the chosen lift displacement 2e2 despite quotient identity.
conjectures.falsifier: A coefficient, operator or history counterexample for the specified interface, or recovery requiring an unrecorded path choice.
conjectures.reopen: A different interface, lift rule or task observation is specified.

conjectures.statement: The declared task selects the toroidal realization, orientation, cyclic mode and reference up to its admitted equivalences.
conjectures.scope: Distinguish one valid construction from an intrinsic or task-selected construction; no uniqueness claim is currently supported.
conjectures.next_test: List remaining choices and their stabilizers. Compare left/right sectors and positive/negative cyclic modes under the same task observations, without enlarging the admitted symmetry group.
conjectures.acceptance: All surviving choices are equivalent under the declared task group, or a source-defined selector distinguishes them.
conjectures.falsifier: Two inequivalent choices satisfy the same task data with no declared selector.
conjectures.reopen: Task observations or admitted equivalences change.

conjectures.statement: An explicit dual comparison presentation transports the full field while recording the change of source fibers.
conjectures.scope: Not the rejected claim that edge duality is a vertex relabelling, and not automatically a native local constructor.
conjectures.next_test: Construct decode/channel-duality/re-encode on the same field and reference. Record which ordered-parent and state-fiber incidences change; compare against a strictly local typed morphism.
conjectures.acceptance: Exact recovery with an explicit transformed incidence contract; any stronger locality claim has its own checked witness.
conjectures.falsifier: Information loss, inconsistent reference transport, or claimed local incidence preservation contradicted by the parent records.
conjectures.reopen: The comparison category or the locality requirement changes.

conjectures.statement: A phase-aware toroidal representation of the selected native N reader task can retain all five coefficients and its declared local structure.
conjectures.scope: Native N uses eighteen two-component patches, unlike P's twelve triples. Equal total dimension is not an incidence identification. Existing phase-dependent seeds are noncanonical.
conjectures.next_test: Specify retained N locality and the phase-dependent binding family before constructing a toroidal encoding. Test two inequivalent admissible seeds for task distinguishability and full-coordinate recovery.
conjectures.acceptance: A declared family of intertwiners preserves the specified task, all five coefficients and absolute origin; any seed freedom is retained or selected explicitly.
conjectures.falsifier: The proposed locality/operator constraints force loss of rank or distinguish choices erased by the encoding.
conjectures.reopen: Binding class, locality or task data change.

conjectures.statement: The toroidal presentations support the selected cross-carrier PN task with explicitly named actions and lifted histories.
conjectures.scope: Do not silently identify the spatial C3 with the internal cycle or revive strict geometric PN equivariance.
conjectures.next_test: After fixing both endpoint interfaces, specify the native PN task and test its full coefficient/operator and path-lift square. If C3 becomes internal on N, name that change in the contract.
conjectures.acceptance: The entire specified diagram commutes without erasing a declared action, coefficient or history.
conjectures.falsifier: The restricted-character obstruction or another explicit residual persists under the stated requirements.
conjectures.reopen: A different cross-carrier task or target action is declared.

decision_trail.result: Twelve directed torus channels give the correct A4 action and decorated field encoding.
decision_trail.consequence: Treat the torus as a concrete field representation, not merely a group analogy.

decision_trail.result: The source paper identifies the b=2 tetrahedral and dual realization alternatives.
decision_trail.consequence: Test their explicit coordinate maps rather than inferring a physical space from the group.

decision_trail.result: Realized left-face sectors recover B and its metric.
decision_trail.consequence: Strengthen the positive relation from decorated indexing to the existing geometric field frames, with choices explicit.

decision_trail.result: The collapsed dual reproduces -B; the faithful cube dual makes that frame recipe singular.
decision_trail.consequence: Keep these as different branches; topology retention and reuse of B are not interchangeable.

decision_trail.result: Operator-preserving channel duality fails endpoint/source-fiber preservation.
decision_trail.consequence: Separate an operator equivalence from a typed comparison morphism.

decision_trail.result: Existing coefficient-binding and strict-PN obstructions constrain proposed transfer lifts.
decision_trail.consequence: Do not schedule already-rejected fixed-N or strict-geometric-PN proposals as fresh unknowns.

decision_trail.result: FCC honeycomb covariance passes; the fixed refinement and fixed global frame fail full A4. Indexed refinements and pose-dependent frames pass their geometric tests.
decision_trail.consequence: Prioritize one explicit refinement-indexed interface under the operator's new spatial proposal. Preserve both positive family results and negative fixed-structure results; do not modify native rules.

decision_trail.result: An eight-sector read-only interface passes exact chart composition, norm and full coefficient/context recovery. Average-only recovery fails; transported NN channels can touch four coarse pairs.
decision_trail.consequence: Close the scoped refinement-interface task. Retain differences, source provenance and the larger operation support. Resume P-reader-lift as the next unchanged frontier task; the N toroidal-incidence question remains distinct from this checked eight-sector comparison.

decision_trail.result: The supplied Chamon paper gives a six-spin octahedral Hamiltonian, four defect classes and a boundary theory retaining normal-derivative data.
decision_trail.consequence: Register five open construction tests. Prioritize the 32-spin periodic stabilizer benchmark; preserve existing verdicts and gate downstream operator and boundary claims on their local checks.

decision_trail.result: Search through ask.sciencemadereadable.com located explicit honeycomb gauge/defect-network constructions, polynomial Clifford maps, coarse-graining circuits and public Chamon stabilizer/syndrome code; targeted full text and code were inspected.
decision_trail.consequence: Reuse these existing constructions. The benchmark becomes an adapter/cross-check task and refinement work starts from the published operator map and gluing rules. Local compatibility verdicts remain unchanged; benchmark priority is retained.

decision_trail.result: Native FCC cells reproduce the signed periodic Chamon algebra and ground spaces; 236 upstream support rows agree. The explicit primitive/Pauli dictionary matches the published Laurent column on 240 octahedra.
decision_trail.consequence: Support the scoped benchmark and polynomial-dictionary nodes. Enable three downstream tasks and prioritize importing the larger operator map for refinement-observable transport; retain actual primitive periods and auxiliary-degree accounting.

decision_trail.result: Appendix B and the supplementary 58-step gate-and-reindexing reduction pass exact checks. Signed lifts on three compatible covers preserve stabilizers and syndromes; four existing charts retain shared-qubit operator products and norms.
decision_trail.consequence: Support the scoped refinement-observables construction. Keep ancilla frames, the sublattice translation and bulk signs explicit. Boundary fields remain gated on defect/boundary rules; no reader lift or quantum-to-neutron coupling is promoted. Spatial/internal symmetry is the next ready task.

maintenance.reason: Import Appendix B and the supplementary reduction, construct signed operator-valued refinement records, and close their scoped algebra/ground-space/syndrome checks.
maintenance.update_rule: For any new test: retain its task and rival class, add a receipt and decisive observable, revise only affected scoped nodes, append the decision trail, recompute readiness and review priorities. A passing checker does not automatically promote a broader hypothesis.
maintenance.priority_review: Review after a frontier test changes a verdict, exposes a new ambiguity, or changes relative effort. Priorities are engineering judgments, not measured probabilities.
